Recovery weighs your heart-rate variability against your personal baseline (~55%%), resting heart rate (~20%%), rest quality (~15%%), respiration (~5%%) and skin-temperature deviation (~5%%). Strain is a 0 - %1$s cardiovascular load from time spent in each heart-rate zone. Sleep is staged from movement and heart rate. The full on-device recompute from the strap\'s raw streams is a later port; the scores below are read from each day\'s cached metrics.
Estimate from today\'s effort, your typical sleep and your %1$s-night recovery baseline - not a measurement. Your real Recovery is scored from tomorrow\'s HRV when you wake.

No scored days yet. Sync your strap to collect raw streams. Strain and Sleep are scored once a day\'s data is in. Recovery needs about four nights of sleep to learn your baseline (you\'ll see \"Calibrating\" until then), and keeps sharpening over your first couple of weeks. On a WHOOP 5 or MG the strap banks little history, so that night count can climb slowly or sit at 0 of 4 until you have worn it across a few nights. That\'s its sync limit, not a fault. Import your WHOOP export to skip the wait.

NOOP gives you three daily scores: Recovery, Strain and Sleep, each from 0 to 100. They are calculated on your device from strap signals and published sport science. They are independent approximations, not WHOOP’s private scores, so the direction may be similar while the numbers differ.

Recovery is led by HRV compared with your personal baseline, plus resting heart rate, last night’s Sleep, breathing rate and skin temperature. Higher HRV means more Recovery. NOOP needs a few nights to learn your baseline; until then it shows “Calibrating”.
Strain: how hard did your heart work?

Strain measures cardiovascular load. Heart rate is converted into a training impulse using heart-rate-reserve zones, with harder zones weighted more heavily, then mapped to a logarithmic 0–100 scale. Steps and active energy provide a floor for long, low-cardio activity.
Sleep: how restorative was your sleep?
Sleep combines sleep duration versus your need, sleep efficiency, restorative deep and REM sleep, and the consistency of sleep and wake times.
Needs %1$d+ consecutive days of Strain to begin. %2$d so far.

Scores Strain on an exponential intensity curve (Banister TRIMP) instead of the default heart-rate zones (Edwards). The default earns nothing below half of your heart-rate reserve, so an hour of lifting — where hard sets average out against the rests — can score close to zero. The exponential curve has no floor and weights short, hard efforts far more heavily. Re-scores your history, and both scales reach the same maximum. Off by default.
Choose when steps and in-progress Strain start over. Naps never start a new day.
